content_blocks.block_data: Unit 2 · Mind Mapping and Creative Thinking Techniques · 120 minutes · studio · COs 109.4, 109.2

slides.speaker_notes: Studio session. Warm-up: Map Your Morning — With No Rules. Do not lecture past 15 minutes.

slides.title: The one idea

content_blocks.block_data: A list hides relationships. A Buzan map shows them — and the laws are what make the difference between a map and a doodle.

slides.speaker_notes: Say it once. Do not elaborate on the slide — elaborate out loud.

slides.title: Why it matters

block_data.body: The brain does not store in lines; it radiates from a centre. A map on paper copies that shape, which is why recall improves.
A central image, not a word. Three colours minimum in that image. Branch thickness heaviest at the centre and thinning outward. Varying letter size.

slides.speaker_notes: Four beats across two slides. Fifteen minutes for all of it.

slides.title: What to do with it

block_data.body: ONE key word per line. Print, do not join up. The word sits on the line. Line length equals word length. Curved branches, never straight rulered ones. Paper landscape.
The main branches off the centre are your BOIs — the four to seven big buckets. Get those right and the rest of the map organises itself.

slides.speaker_notes: Four beats across two slides. Fifteen minutes for all of it.

slides.title: Today you will

content_blocks.block_data: Draw a Buzan-compliant map of your anchor enterprise, twice.
